finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::datasource "ssl" option disables tls certificate verification (`rejectunauthorized: false`), while the newly added doc presents it as a security toggle
evidence: In the supplied packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts, createClient() literally builds `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false` with `password: decrypt(ds.password)` on the adjacent line, so enabling "SSL" encrypts but never validates the server certificate — an on-path attacker can MITM and capture the decrypted DB credentials and results. The PR does add packages/documentation/sheets/datasources.md with "**SSL** — toggle on if your database requires it", documenting that toggle without any caveat, so the claim's factual basis holds. Two mitigating notes: the insecure TLS setting is pre-existing and untouched by this diff (only the doc is new), and the doc wording is neutral rather than an explicit security promise, so "presents it as a security toggle" is slightly overstated. I could not verify the exact line number (204) since no checkout is mounted, but the code content is exactly as cited.
